prostaflush.texto: The main challenge was creating copy and visual hooks to capture users, as well as working with several video files using AI, trying to make the AI output as flawless as possible to keep the viewer engaged throughout the sales video. Experimenting with different AI video-generation tools led me to solve problems along the way.

vortex.texto: The main challenge on this project was using React Native with Expo, since I had only worked with React Native without Expo, creating routes manually. The main problems I faced during development were related to adjusting the positioning of interface elements and responsiveness between Android and iOS, but my solid background in HTML5 and CSS3 helped me a lot in solving these problems.

crm.texto: The main challenges working with Microsoft's Dynamics 365 CRM were its far-from-intuitive interface: a very robust system with countless functions and possibilities. At the time, AI tools weren't nearly as capable as they are today, especially for anything specific to Dynamics 365. I ran into problems of many kinds within the platform, such as database issues, field relationships and integrations, and I usually had to solve them by reading Microsoft's own documentation or requesting meetings with Microsoft specialists, who were often based abroad, so I communicated in English to work through the issues.

pesse.texto: The main challenge at Pesse was designing an interface for fleet managers to use, since most of them had limited familiarity with technology. I managed to create interfaces built on accessibility principles, making the platform flexible and efficient, which greatly eased its use during field logistics operations.

besalt.texto: The main challenges during my time as an entrepreneur at Besalt: first, since it was a partnership, I had to adapt to my partners' pace. As a partner, I felt responsible for stepping in wherever the company needed: I was the sales rep, product owner, UI/UX designer, scrum master, content creator, social media manager and front-end developer. Because I had both product and technical knowledge, I could assess the feasibility of implementing client requirements right there in sales meetings, which streamlined the client-development workflow and prevented problems from surfacing later during development.

labLider.subtitulo: University of Fortaleza – Innovation Lab (Design Lead)
labLider.texto: The main challenges at Unifor's Innovation Lab, as design lead, were gathering requirements with clients, analyzing them, and handing them off to the product design team to build interface prototypes aligned with each project's goal and scope. During this period I began studying HCI in depth, including Nielsen's heuristics and Donald Norman's teachings, which changed how I saw the world and technology and helped me streamline the workflow between client, designer and developer, solving scope-creep and requirement issues as they came up.

labEstagiario.subtitulo: University of Fortaleza – Innovation Lab (UI & UX Design Intern)
labEstagiario.texto: During my first year as an intern, I worked on a wide range of activities: 3D modeling, 2D and 3D animation, digital drawing, iconography, visual identity, interface prototyping, graphic design, print design, HTML and CSS, writing scientific papers, and academic research and development. From the second year on, I realized my potential was really in creating interfaces using the best practices of interaction design and user experience. The biggest problems I faced in this period were designing interfaces that were too complex for developers to implement, since I didn't yet have enough technical knowledge. That's when I started studying front-end development more seriously, mainly to make communication between designer and developer easier.

consentimento.usoOHotjarPara: I use Hotjar to understand how the site is browsed (clicks, scrolling and anonymous session recordings) and improve the experience. It only runs with your consent.

privacidade.leiGeralDeProtecao: Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD, Law 13.709/2018)
privacidade.corpo:
Controller: Aglalberto Silva — ux@aglalberto.com.

What is collected: with your consent, Hotjar (Contentsquare) records browsing data — pages viewed, clicks, scrolling, mouse movements, device and browser type, screen resolution and approximate location — and records sessions anonymously. This site has no forms and never asks for your name, e-mail or other identifying data.

Why: only to understand how the portfolio is used and improve the experience. Data is not sold or used for advertising.

Cookieless statistics: Umami counts visits and button clicks (e.g. "View project", "Behavioral profile") in an aggregated, anonymous way, with no cookies and without identifying visitors. It runs regardless of your choice above.

Legal basis: consent (LGPD art. 7, I) for Hotjar, which only loads if you accept; legitimate interest (art. 7, IX) for Umami's anonymous statistics.

Local storage: your browser keeps your language, theme (light/dark) and privacy choices. If you accept, Hotjar sets its own analytics cookies. When you play the video, the Vimeo player may use its own cookies.

Your rights: you can change your choice at any time here or via the "Privacy" link in the footer, and you can request access, correction or deletion of data through the e-mail above (LGPD art. 18).
